question: At matched request and CPU budgets on the same versioned REST APIs, does coverage-level-guided black-box fuzzing find more independently reproduced distinct faults than unguided mutations?
competing_hypotheses: Coverage-level feedback yields more distinct reproducible faults per budget.
Any apparent gain is due to different request validity, API mix, or compute spend.
falsifying_experiment: Pin API versions and fuzzer code; randomize paired seeds/order; equalize requests and CPU; blind-deduplicate and rerun fault candidates; compare paired distinct-bug yield and valid-request rate.

later_evidence.relationship: Related API-fuzzing improvements, but white-box heuristics and different systems do not directly settle the matched black-box feedback question.
Related black-box RL API fuzzer; single reported API and no matched head-to-head answer to this question.

selection_note: Derived from an actually sampled 2021 year-end-safe abstract; wording is our testable formulation, not a quotation from the author. Later evidence was located with a post-cutoff search and is excluded from forecast features.

question: Do versioned corrections to NVD metadata measurably improve prospective vulnerability-prioritization decisions, compared with the uncorrected NVD snapshot at the same cutoff?
competing_hypotheses: Corrected dates, products and severity fields improve prospective triage against independently verified outcomes.
Corrections alter retrospective statistics but do not improve prospective triage once coverage and workload are matched.
falsifying_experiment: Snapshot NVD and correction rules at a historical cutoff; blind future verified exploit/patch outcomes; compare matched triage policies with fixed alert budget and stratified product groups.

later_evidence.relationship: NVD user interview/survey reports missing or incorrect entries; it does not test prospective correction benefit and is outside the predeclared three-year window.

selection_note: Derived from an actually sampled 2020 year-end-safe abstract; NVD source reports data problems, not demonstrated prospective security benefit. Later evidence is not a historical forecast label.

question: Across independent projects and framework versions, do predictive-SE model rankings remain stable when cross-validation folds and random seeds are rerun?
competing_hypotheses: Rankings remain unstable under plausible reruns and library changes.
Rankings stabilize after harmonizing splits, tuning and reported uncertainty.
falsifying_experiment: Freeze dataset versions, resampling and hyperparameters; rerun at least 30 predeclared seeds and two library implementations on held-out projects; measure rank reversals and uncertainty before opening a held-out test set.

later_evidence.relationship: Related review of deep-learning software fault-prediction reproducibility, not a direct rank-stability replication and outside the three-year window.

selection_note: Derived from an actually sampled 2020 year-end-safe abstract. The later systematic review is contextual evidence, not resolution of this quantitative question.
